task_interpretation.use_case_description: Detect traffic participants in each image for local traffic monitoring on a MacBook Air with Apple M4 using CPU/Metal.

available_hardware.details: Apple M4 CPU; Metal acceleration; local inference

model.description: Chosen YOLO11s for CPU/Metal deployment on Apple Silicon (M4). It delivers the strongest mAP50-95 at 640 input among CPU-friendly options in the retrieved set, with a very small inference memory footprint and a favorable CPU-on-CPU path in available benchmarks. This aligns with the target mAP>=0.30 and the constraint of running on CPU/Metal on a MacBook Air.

model_selection.rationale: The traffic-monitoring task benefits from high mAP@0.5:0.95 and efficient CPU inference. YOLO11s provides the best combination of accuracy (mAP50-95 ~47.0 on COCO at 640), compact memory footprint (~0.27 GB VRAM-equivalent), and mature documentation/evidence. Other strong CPU-friendly options (YOLov10s, YOLOv8s) offer competitive accuracy but slightly lower mAP or less favorable CPU-path benchmarks in the supplied data. Given the local, CPU/Metal deployment constraint and the ~0.3 target mAP, YOLO11s is the most robust single pick from the retrieved candidates. Fall-back options would be YOLOv10s or YOLOv8s if hardware or integration constraints favor slightly different latency/throughput profiles.

advantages: Highest mAP50-95 among CPU-friendly options in the set (COCO 640 input: 47.0).
Low inference memory footprint (total_estimated_vram_gb about 0.272).
Compact model size with strong documentation and community support (YOLO11 docs and evidence).
risks: CPU latency on Apple Silicon Metal path is not explicitly benchmarked in the data; real-world latency may vary with the specific Mac/driver setup.
Small-object/AP-small performance data is not provided; cannot claim AP-small superiority without direct evidence.

risks: CPU-specific latency benchmarks are not fully defined in the data; performance on Mac M4/Metal is inferred rather than measured here.
Slightly lower mAP than YOLO11s; may be a tie-breaker if latency is critical.

advantages: Strong overall performance (mAP50-95 44.9) with robust ecosystem and tooling.

risks: Lower accuracy than YOLO11s in the provided data, which could matter for harder small-object cases.

available_hardware.details: MacBook Air with Apple M4, unified memory, CPU/Metal acceleration

model.description: YOLOv11N variant optimized for CPU/Metal on macOS (Apple M4). Balances high mAP@0.5:0.95 with a very small on-device memory footprint and favorable CPU latency. Evidence suggests mAP50-95 around 39.5 on COCO at 640 input size, with CPU-ONNX latency benchmarks (~56 ms per image) and inference memory around 0.256 GB. Well suited for traffic camera car detection on a MacBook-like CPU/Metal path; robust across varied lighting and occlusion.

model_selection.rationale: YOLOv11N offers the strongest combination of high accuracy and very small inference memory among the CPU-friendly candidates, while demonstrating practical CPU-on-CPU latency well below the 500 ms hard cap. Its 640 input size aligns with common traffic-camera resolutions, and its MAP50-95 (~39.5) comfortably exceeds the target threshold. Although on-device Metal acceleration specifics are not directly provided in the evidence, the CPU-ONNX latency benchmarks and model-memory estimates indicate a feasible on-Mac deployment path. The main risk is that real-world on-Mac performance with Metal may differ from CPU/ONNX benchmarks; this should be validated in a lightweight on-device test. If on-device constraints are tighter than expected, a slower but memory-compact option such as SSD300 can be considered as a fallback, trading some accuracy for simplicity and stability on extremely constrained setups.

model.description: YOLOv11s small, fast variant with strong mAP@0.5:0.95 and low inference memory; chosen for dense urban scenes with small objects and a target mAP>=0.3, while meeting memory and latency constraints on a MacBook Air with M4 (Metal acceleration).

model_selection.rationale: Chosen YOLO11s due to the best practical balance for this task among the graph candidates that satisfy the hard filters. YOLO11s offers the highest reported mAP50-95 among the two evaluated options (47.0 on COCO-640), while keeping a very small memory footprint (~0.272 GB) and low latency potential on optimized runtimes. This aligns with the target mAP>=0.3 and a 0.5 s per-frame goal, given that even CPU/ONNX benchmarks for similar lightweight YOLO variants are below 0.5 s. YOLO11n, while very lightweight, provides lower accuracy (39.5 map50-95) and thus represents a weaker trade-off for this use case. Other candidates (Faster R-CNN, RetinaNet, SSD300) generally incur higher compute or offering lower small-object performance in practice, making them less favorable under the stated constraints. Uncertainties remain around Apple M4/Metal-specific on-device benchmarks and AP-small measurements for these variants; real-world validation on the target hardware is recommended for final confirmation.

task_interpretation.use_case_description: Identify traffic lights and traffic signs in dense urban street scenes.

model.description: YOLOv11s chosen as the primary model for detecting traffic lights and traffic signs in dense urban scenes with small objects. It has a strong COCO benchmark showing high mAP50-95 (~47.0) at input size around 640, while maintaining a very small inference memory footprint (~0.27 GB in FP16) suitable for a RTX 2060 with 6 GB, and low to moderate latency. This aligns well with the requirement of small object detection in dense scenes and keeps memory well under the 6 GB limit.

model_selection.rationale: The primary goal is high detection quality for small objects (traffic lights and signs) in dense urban scenes while staying within a 6 GB inference memory budget. Among the retrieved candidates, YOLOv11s offers the best balance of high mAP@0.5:0.95 on COCO, small memory footprint, and strong small-object performance, which is most relevant to the target domain. Other competitive options such as YOLOv10s provide similarly strong results with slightly different trade-offs, and Faster R-CNN variants provide robust localization but at higher memory/latency and often lower mAP50-95 in these contexts. The chosen YOLO11s model thus best fits the performance requirements and deployment constraints for the RTX 2060 setup.</narrative>

It should handle cluttered rooms, partial occlusion, varied lighting, and objects viewed from different angles. Inference will run on CPU-only backend servers with approximately 8 CPU cores and 16 GB of RAM. The model should aim for a mAP@0.5:0.95 of approximately 0.30 or higher.

The chosen model provides a favorable accuracy/efficiency trade-off for CPU-only inference and the target mAP. Potential caveats include CPU latency variability by input size and environment; if latency becomes prohibitive, consider a smaller variant (yolov10s) or a faster-detection path (yolov10n) as fallbacks.
